description: Figure 5 presents two pie charts side by side, each depicting the error analysis for a different model: the Vanilla model on the left and the HCL model on the right. The left pie chart is divided into three segments: a large dark teal section labeled “Atomic Skill Fail” at 68.0%, a medium-sized light blue section labeled “Correct” at 21.0%, and a small white section labeled “Question Misunderstood” at 8.0%. The right pie chart is divided into four segments: a large dark teal section labeled “Atomic Skill Fail” at 10.0%, a medium-sized light blue section labeled “Correct” at 55.0%, a smaller light gray section labeled “Reason Error” at 14.0%, and a small white section labeled “Question Misunderstood” at 2.0%. Both charts use color-coded segments to represent different error categories, with percentage values explicitly labeled within each slice. The charts are visually distinct in their proportions, showing a higher proportion of “Correct” responses for the HCL model compared to the Vanilla model, and a higher proportion of “Atomic Skill Fail” for the Vanilla model.
